decisions.question: Approve deadline-driven blocking flush barriers within the sink, or expand scope to add asynchronous storage completion notifications?
decisions.why_approval_required: The FixTask requires approval for important behavior changes and edits outside allowed paths; AGENTS.md:20 independently requires approval. An aged-batch barrier can block the worker before the configured flush deadline, affecting queue pressure. Removing maintenance completion checks also changes idle failure-observation timing. Calling poll only at the batch deadline is insufficient under saturation: it can retain the overdue batch without exposing a notification to await.

options.description: Modify only sinks/mod.rs and sinks/mcap.rs: expose the next actual deadline, wait for packets/disconnect or that deadline, and call flush_written at the earlier of the storage batch deadline and configured flush deadline. Remove maintenance-driven writer.poll calls and retain poisoning, ordered writes, rotation, and finish barriers.
benefits: Smallest repair using existing documented APIs, with no dependency or configuration additions.
Retains batching and the one-second batch-age trigger; completion waits use the existing kernel-backed barrier.
Keeps configured flush deadlines from being postponed by earlier batch flushes.
tradeoffs: Aged-batch flushing becomes blocking and can increase queue pressure when storage is slow.

Idle completion failures are observed at the next submission or barrier rather than maintenance checks; outstanding writes without a buffered batch can await the configured deadline, which permits up to 60 seconds.

options.description: Expand authorization to the storage writer, MCAP API, and relevant tests. Add a completion/capacity notification interface and let the sink wait on notifications, packets, disconnect, and real flush deadlines.
benefits: Preserves asynchronous aged-batch submission and prompt completion/failure handling.
Allows an overdue batch to await capacity without repeated timer polling.
tradeoffs: Requires out-of-scope storage API changes and substantially more lifecycle and concurrency work.
Requires validation of notification races, deferred kernel work, saturation, rotation, failure, and shutdown.
